The mysterious, almost religious tone that builds up actual dread, and the concept of the normally stoic and fearless Council being so terrified and apologetic to this unknown force is a brilliant idea. -1, but the idea is solid. Putting a serious idea on the buildup could make a fantastic mainlister. Perhaps you could even turn this silly concept into a serious idea, à la 5004.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Novote, because I'm a bit conflicted on this.

I second the thoughts that the joke is a bit too on-the-nose and when it's revealed it feels kinda disappointing. In an odd way, this doesn't feel like a good anticlimactic ending to me, even though it's very anticlimactic in its core, and sorta fulfills its purpose. I think it's because it doesn't leave you with a sense of "oh shit gottem" feeling, just a bit of unironical disappointment regarding the fact that such a cool setup led to this. I think it would've worked better if it wasn't about the typical stolen food trope/the punchline though, even if the stinger would have a similar purpose. Dunno, it felt like that last sentence just didn't fit with the buildup in any way.

That said, I can also see how well it works when you look at it as a parody of typical over-the-top O5 stuff that takes place in some serious articles. It can be perceived as a pretty hilarious jab, and in that sense it does work quite well.

item.content:encoded:
I've decided to no-vote this. The punchline feels like it doesn't have adequate setup and flies in the face of the rest of the article's tone. While that disjointed tone is the point of the joke and the punchline ostensibly appears to be "out of left field", it ended up being rather predictable. This may have been more impactful if I came to this article without knowing it was supposed to be a -J. Super serious and wrathful tone from the unnamed character + knowing this is a -J = me expecting the unnamed character to be pissed about something petty. Ultimately, it doesn't surprise me or subvert that expectation and the expectation itself wasn't enough to carry this for me.

Edit: per the other commenters, I very much enjoyed the buildup you provided. It added a sense of dread incrementally in a manner that would make Stephen King proud. Unfortunately, it still feels like a disjointed end tacted on to a wonderful progression of tension.
